items.q: In the nephron transport schematic, which transporter in the thick ascending limb of Henle establishes the lumen-positive potential that drives paracellular calcium and magnesium reabsorption?
o: NKCC2 Na+-K+-2Cl- cotransporter with ROMK potassium recycling
items.exp: The NKCC2 cotransporter reabsorbs 1 Na+, 1 K+ and 2 Cl- electroneutrally. However, back-leakage of K+ into the tubular lumen via apical ROMK channels creates an lumen-positive transepithelial potential of approximately +8 mV, which repels and drives paracellular reabsorption of divalent cations Ca2+ and Mg2+. Loop diuretics inhibit NKCC2, abolishing this potential and causing hypercalciuria.
r: Incorrect. SGLT2 is located in the proximal tubule.
Correct. NKCC2 combined with ROMK potassium back-leak generates the lumen-positive driving potential.
Incorrect. NCCT is electroneutral and located in the distal convoluted tubule.
Incorrect. ENaC creates a lumen-negative potential in collecting ducts.
items.kp: ROMK potassium back-leak in the thick ascending limb generates a lumen-positive potential driving Ca2+ and Mg2+ reabsorption.
